scopeDecisions.decision: Closure is defined by these behavioral acceptance conditions, observed through the REST surface (Identity Toolkit and Secure Token) on the disposable Identity Platform sandbox, as for AUTH-ACCOUNT and AUTH-CREDENTIAL. Every action code is generated through the Admin accounts:sendOobCode with returnOobLink, which returns the code and mails no code (applying an email change may still notify the old address; every corpus address is @example.com, which publishes a null MX, so nothing is delivered); the client accounts:sendOobCode is observed only for a PASSWORD_RESET of an address that has no account. Mail delivery itself (templates, sender, localization, the message a client request would send) is not emulated by any parent: local development does not need it (owner, 2026-09-24). Client and Admin SDK paths belong to AUTH-CONFIG-SDK, as AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A5.

An action link is compared by its query parameters (mode, oobCode as the answer's own code, apiKey by presence, continueUrl, lang and any other). Where its handler lives is not compared: production links to the project's hosted action page and fireemu to its own /emulator/action handler, as the official emulator does, because a local link must reach the emulator. The hosted page's browser flow is out of scope.
Action codes are opaque credentials: their value and length are not compared. Production codes are 54-character base64url strings; fireemu's are its own identifiers.
Tenant-scoped action codes and links belong to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING, as AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A8; blocking functions (beforeSendEmail, beforeSignIn on an email-link sign-in) belong there too.

Mobile link settings (iOSBundleId, androidPackageName, androidInstallApp, androidMinimumVersion, dynamicLinkDomain, linkDomain) belong to AUTH-CONFIG-SDK; this parent observes continueUrl and canHandleCodeInApp.

The project's authorized domains decide whether an action-code continueUrl is accepted: the strict profile refuses one outside them with UNAUTHORIZED_DOMAIN, as production does, and the emulator profile adds no refusal (the official emulator checks no domain). fireemu's Admin config carries authorizedDomains, by default localhost and the project's firebaseapp.com and web.app domains; the harness requires the sandbox's configured list (its two Hosting domains, without localhost) in production and gives it to fireemu through the same Admin config. Email-link sign-in is observed with signIn.email.passwordRequired switched off for the email-link programs only; the harness restores and reads it back after each program and checks the whole sign-in baseline at the start and end of a recording.
Any HTTP 429 or quota refusal in this corpus is classified INDETERMINATE; quotas belong to AUTH-CONFIG-SDK, as AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A7.
The ID-token claims and refresh of an email-link session are required conditions here (AUTH-CREDENTIAL scope decision C7); token refusals after a password reset or an email change are counted here.

The final-artifact regression re-runs the AUTH-ACCOUNT and AUTH-CREDENTIAL corpora and inherits their one documented divergence: AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A12, the gson parser message text for malformed customAttributes JSON.

conditions.note: Admin sendOobCode with returnOobLink for every request type: answer members, link parameters, continueUrl on authorized, unauthorized, malformed and empty values, canHandleCodeInApp, unknown, disabled and mixed-case addresses, missing and unknown request types, missing and invalid addresses, the new address of an email change (missing, taken, the same, invalid), email-link generation while password sign-in is required, and codes selected by an ID token instead of an address. The Admin email-change generator reads only the address (MISSING_EMAIL for an ID token alone), so the inspection row after it records only that dependency.
The client sendOobCode for an address that has no account (improved email privacy on): the plain request, returnOobLink on the client route, continueUrl checks and a missing API key.

Password reset codes: inspection without use, weak and empty passwords, missing, unknown and truncated codes, use and reuse, a newer code retiring an older one, sign-in with the old and new password, tokens issued before the reset, the account after the reset, and codes issued before an Admin or client password change, an email change, a disable (and re-enable) and a deletion; a verification code offered as a reset code.

Email verification codes: inspection, apply and reapply, tokens and refresh after verification, unknown and truncated codes, an already verified address, codes issued before an email change, a disable (the refusal keeps the code) and a deletion, and a reset code applied as a verification. Whether a newer verification code retires an older one is unobserved: production refuses a second verification link for an address within minutes (TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS_TRY_LATER), so the corpus gives each link an address of its own, and fireemu keeps every verification code.

VERIFY_AND_CHANGE_EMAIL codes: inspection, a newer code and the older one, apply and reapply, sign-in by the old and new addresses, tokens and refresh issued before the change, the new address taken before use, the account's address changed, disabled or deleted before use, a change code offered as a reset code, and a verification code of the old address applied after the change.

Email-link sign-in: generation (continueUrl and canHandleCodeInApp), inspection, a mismatched, missing or mixed-case address, missing and unknown codes, a new and an existing account, reuse, a newer link and the older one, a link refused for a disabled account (so its sign-in row records only that dependency) and a deleted account, linking the address to an anonymous session, to a session whose address differs, and an address another account owns, codes of the other types on the email-link route and the email-link code on the other routes, and a password reset of an account that only ever signed in by link.

The ID token of an email-link sign-in (new account, existing password account, anonymous session linked by link): header and claims including firebase.sign_in_provider and identities, the refresh of that session, a lookup, and a session cookie made from it (AUTH-CREDENTIAL scope decision C7).

Legacy ID tokens (a password sign-in without returnSecureToken): a VERIFY_EMAIL link selected by a legacy token on the Admin route, email-link linking with a legacy token, and the client sendOobCode of a VERIFY_AND_CHANGE_EMAIL with a legacy and with a secure token (owner decision 2026-09-24), which production accepts. The Admin route's email-change generator reads only the address (MISSING_EMAIL), so its code and application rows depend on a step that returned nothing and record only that dependency; the client row is the evidence that a legacy token selects an email change.
Whose code it is: a verification or change code of one account applied with another account's ID token or a garbage token, and a reset code checked and used while naming another account's address.

A PASSWORD_RESET code about ten seconds before and after its one-hour lifetime (inspection, use, a second account's code, and a new code afterwards; production answers EXPIRED_OOB_CODE); VERIFY_EMAIL, VERIFY_AND_CHANGE_EMAIL and EMAIL_SIGNIN codes inspected and used after the same hour. Their full lifetime is unobserved (owner decision 2026-09-24): the recording shows them live at about 3,610 s, the exploration at 3,900 s. No Google document states their lifetime (searched 2026-09-25: the Admin email-action-link, email-link sign-in and GetOobCodeResponse references), so fireemu's strict profile never refuses them as expired (owner decision 2026-09-25); at the per-project cap of outstanding codes the oldest of them older than 3,900 s makes room. An expired PASSWORD_RESET code is kept a day to be refused as expired (an inference). Exploration before the recording (not evidence): docs.local/runs/auth-action-explore-20260924/lifetime-*.jsonl.
Every AUTH-ACTION, AUTH-CREDENTIAL and AUTH-ACCOUNT row compared on one final artifact, with the Rust workspace tests of that source.

documentedDivergences.reason: AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A12: production returns gson's parser message for malformed customAttributes JSON; the INVALID_CLAIMS refusal itself matches.
